business_problem: i GRID LAB needed to collect and analyze renewable-energy, demand, battery, and EV data quickly enough to predict surplus power and automate device control, while proving the concept fast in a rapidly changing energy market.
solution_summary: i GRID LAB built the R.E.A.L. New Energy Platform on AWS to predict and control surplus renewable power using IoT data and AI. Distributed Energy Resource data—including solar generation, demand, storage-battery status, and EV charging and discharging—is collected from edge devices with AWS IoT Greengrass and stored in the cloud for high-speed time-series processing with Amazon Timestream. AI functions migrated onto Amazon SageMaker then combine that operational data with external inputs such as electricity market prices to forecast excess solar generation, determine optimal EV charging and discharging timing, and create automated control scenarios. The result is a serverless-oriented platform that can move from proof of concept to commercialization quickly while supporting regional power-circulation use cases, logistics decarbonization, and broader green-transformation programs.

solution_components.name: AWS IoT Greengrass
solution_components.role: Collects data from edge devices connected to energy assets and facilities.

solution_components.name: Amazon Timestream
solution_components.role: Processes and stores large volumes of time-series energy data at high speed.

solution_components.name: Amazon SageMaker
solution_components.role: Runs the AI functions used for surplus-power prediction and automatic control decisions.

solution_components.name: AWS IoT Core
solution_components.role: Supports the cloud-side IoT connectivity and messaging environment referenced by the case-study service list.

data_flow: Solar, demand, battery, and EV telemetry is collected from edge devices through AWS IoT Greengrass into the cloud, processed as time-series data in Amazon Timestream, combined with external information such as electricity market prices in SageMaker-based AI models, and then used to generate automatic control scenarios for distributed energy resources.
business_outcome: i GRID LAB built the proof of concept in 6 months, published first results 1 month later, expanded to around 500 solar facilities and about 100,000 households, and created a commercial platform to support regional green power circulation and future GX cities.
metrics: 10 GX cities with 100 percent renewable energy using this platform
architecture_clues: Uses a serverless framework to shorten coding and documentation time.
